function: Symbol detection of on-off keyed signals in a 2x2 molecular MIMO link with a feedforward neural network preceded by derivative and sliding modules (p. 3).
system: 2x2 molecular MIMO prototype (p. 2), spatial multiplexing with OOK, diffusion channel at 90 to 120 cm (p. 3); no RIS; no RF band, chemical signals.
method: Feedforward NN with two hidden layers of 5 sigmoid nodes, derivative preprocessing and sliding module; supervised offline training with cross-entropy loss (pp. 3-4).
data_channel: Experimental CIR realizations of the molecular MIMO prototype of [15] at several distances, convolved with random bit sequences of length 30,000, for training and testing (pp. 3-4).
test_conditions: Dataset split randomly 50% training and 50% testing, with 10-fold cross-validation; tested at 120 cm for symbol durations of 10 to 15 s; no unseen scenario (p. 4).
baselines: Model-based NDbD, SDbD and RED [7]; learned symbol-by-symbol FNN, sequence FNN-2 and SBRNN-2 of [9] (pp. 4-5).
metrics: BER versus symbol duration (Fig. 4, p. 5); complexity order (Table I) and training time in seconds (Table II) (p. 4).
complexity: Table I gives complexity orders of FNN, FNN-K, SBRNN-K and CMDD; Table II gives training times, CMDD 0.4826 s for 5 epochs (p. 4).
q1_support: p. 3: "The dataset in the training step is obtained by the experimental platform established in [15]"
q2_support: p. 4: "the training set accounts for the 50% of the data, and the testing set takes up the rest 50%"; no unseen scenario, distance, symbol duration or dataset is tested.
q3_support: p. 4: "the native derivative-based detector (NDbD)"; p. 4: "the SBRNN is characterized by a solitary BiLSTM layer in its hidden structure [9]"; p. 5: "Comparison of the BER performance among the CMDD"
q4_support: p. 4: "Table I summarizes the computational complexities of the NNs mentioned"; p. 4: "Table II summarizes the computational time required for training FNN, SBRNN, and our proposed CMDD methods"
q5_support: p. 1: "validated through experimental data from a molecular MIMO prototype"; met only by the measured-data route, since no link, DOI or release statement for code or data appears in the paper.
notes: Molecular communication (diffusion of molecules), not an RF link: the MIMO is a 2x2 molecular prototype (p. 2), so the reviewer should confirm that it falls within area 1 (MIMO detection); included because the learned NN recovers the symbols of a multi-transmitter, multi-receiver link (p. 3). q1 and q5 rest on measured CIRs of the prototype of [15]; the received signals are synthesized by convolving those CIRs with random bits (p. 3), so the reviewer should confirm that this counts as measured data. The paper gives no code or data link. q2: random 50/50 split plus 10-fold cross-validation (p. 4); the comparison with RED on the dataset of [7] (p. 5) does not state that CMDD was trained on other data. q3: SBRNN-2 of [9] is the earlier learned baseline (p. 4, Fig. 4 on p. 5); NDbD, SDbD and RED are the non-learned baselines. In Table II, the asterisk marks a variant with the derivatives module (p. 4).
